stances.claim: CJ is overwhelmed by congratulations for the Pro Ecclesia et Pontifice award granted by Pope Francis but considers himself 'just an ordinary worker in the Lord's Vineyard'; during the Sept 18 Manila Cathedral Mass presided by Cardinal Advincula, he said the award does not belong to him.

The award belongs first to those who undertook the four Rs -- retrofitting, restrengthening, restoration, and renovation -- of the Manila Cathedral over 2012-2015, all of whom preferred anonymity per Matthew 6:1 until the Vicar of Christ acclaimed their work.

The renovation involved bringing down the 17-ton belfry bells in 2010 (replaced by 23 lighter computerized Carillon bells from the Netherlands), Cardinal Tagle's 2012 decision to close the structurally weakened church, and -- despite the absence of 'as-built' plans -- verbal-trust generosity from named donor families (Ang, the late Ty, Ayala brothers, the Linas, and an anonymous donor), with DM Consunji as general contractor donating its margins.

The center columns, weakened by time, were reinforced by structural engineer Angel Lazaro's team under Salvador Castro using countless rolls of carbon fiber and gallons of epoxy, with marble covers carefully chipped off and restored without breakage -- 'the miracle is that none of the marble covers broke or fragmented' -- and floor marble lifted to lay underlying drainage, plumbing, and electrical systems.

The award also belongs to those who walked with CJ in his spiritual journey -- his family, SC brethren, FLP, FLP Scholars Society, the Bukas Loob sa Diyos Covenant Community -- and specifically to the late Fr Michael Nolan, who as FEU chaplain snatched CJ as 'youngest president of the FEU Central Student Organization' from the lures of Marxism and helped him organize the National Union of Students against the Marxist-leaning student movements of the time.

Special acknowledgment goes to his late Leni, who 'set aside her vocation to be a Benedictine nun to marry undeserving me,' and to former envoy to the Holy See Tita de Villa, who gently ushered CJ to the inner sanctum of the Church, introduced him to bishops, and got him elected to lay-leadership roles including the Vatican-based Pontifical Council for the Laity.

CJ also hailed CJ Gesmundo for foregoing a Bangkok judicial conference to attend, and Tessie Sy Coson -- former Assumption commercial-law student -- whose rise to her career's summit has left her 'simple, modest, unaffected, and unassuming.'

Finally, CJ reiterated the 1995 vow he delivered upon entering the SC without prior judicial or public office: 'I hold office by God's grace, and I pledge to serve Him and our people with fortitude, integrity, competence, and prudence. I dedicate all that I am, and all that I will ever be, to Him who is the Source of everything.' To God Be the Glory!

notable_anecdotes: The 17-ton belfry bells brought down in 2010 and replaced by 23 lighter computerized Carillon bells from the Netherlands -- a concrete engineering detail that grounds an otherwise spiritual column in the physics of cathedral preservation.

Cardinal Tagle's 2012 decision to close the structurally weakened church 'lest, heaven forbid, it toppled down due to an earthquake' upon assuming the Manila archbishopric -- and Tagle's later text to CJ from his Vatican posting: 'always treasure the communion and collaboration.'

The absence-of-as-built-plans detail -- donors and contractors proceeding 'without written plans and sometimes without any written requests' on verbal assurances -- a striking trust-based account of the renovation.

The named-donor enumeration with personal modifiers ('Don Ramon Ang,' 'the late Dr. George S.K. Ty,' 'the brothers Jaime Augusto and Fernando Zobel de Ayala,' 'the spouses Bert and Sylvia Lina,' 'a kind donor who preferred to remain anonymous') -- preserving the specific generosity rather than aggregating it.
The 'miracle' that none of the marble covers broke or fragmented during the restoration -- recorded in CJ's own voice as a marker of providential success.

The Fr Michael Nolan anecdote -- 'snatched me, as the youngest president of the FEU Central Student Organization, from the lures of Marxism' -- also told in earlier columns (A15) but here folded into the spiritual-credit register and paired with the National Union of Students organizing detail.

The Leni-Benedictine-nun detail -- 'my late Leni who set aside her vocation to be a Benedictine nun to marry undeserving me' -- one of the most personally tender phrasings in CJ's late columns, with the 'undeserving me' continuing the column's humility-disclaimer motif.

Tessie Sy Coson -- 'who my Leni and I have admired since she was my student in commercial law at the Assumption College... she has remained simple, modest, unaffected, and unassuming' -- a memoir-detail that maps the SM-Group connection back to a teacher-student relationship.
The 1995 SC vow recited verbatim -- paired with the four-virtues compound (fortitude, integrity, competence, prudence) as the operative judicial-character formulation.
The 'To God Be the Glory!' close -- a doxological exclamation rare for CJ even in spiritual columns, signaling the column's hymnic register.

one_paragraph_summary: Overwhelmed by congratulations on the Pro Ecclesia et Pontifice award conferred by Pope Francis, Panganiban -- 'just an ordinary worker in the Lord's Vineyard' -- used the Sept 18 Manila Cathedral Mass presided by Cardinal Advincula to redirect the honor to others. First, to those behind the four Rs -- retrofitting, restrengthening, restoration, and renovation -- undertaken from 2012 to 2015, who preferred anonymity per Matthew 6:1 until the Vicar of Christ acclaimed their work: the relocation of the 17-ton belfry bells in 2010 (replaced by 23 lighter computerized Carillon bells from the Netherlands); Cardinal Tagle's 2012 decision upon assuming the Manila archbishopric to close the structurally weakened church lest it topple in an earthquake; and the verbal-trust generosity (without 'as-built' plans, sometimes without written requests) of donor families -- Don Ramon Ang, the late Dr. George S.K. Ty, the brothers Jaime Augusto and Fernando Zobel de Ayala, the Linas, and an anonymous donor -- with DM Consunji's Sid Consunji donating margins. Structural engineer Angel Lazaro and supervisor Salvador Castro reinforced the weakened center columns with carbon fiber and epoxy after chipping off marble covers that were later restored without breakage ('the miracle is that none of the marble covers broke or fragmented'); marble floors were lifted to lay drainage, plumbing, and electrical, with sound and lighting modernized. Second, to those who walked CJ's spiritual journey -- his family, SC brethren, FLP, FLP Scholars Society, the Bukas Loob sa Diyos Covenant Community -- and specifically the late Fr Michael Nolan who as FEU chaplain snatched the impoverished CJ, then youngest president of the FEU Central Student Organization, from Marxist temptation and helped him organize the National Union of Students; the late Leni, who 'set aside her vocation to be a Benedictine nun to marry undeserving me'; former envoy to the Holy See Tita de Villa, who ushered CJ into the inner sanctum of the Church including the Vatican-based Pontifical Council for the Laity; CJ Gesmundo, who foregoing a Bangkok judicial conference to attend; and Tessie Sy Coson, his former Assumption commercial-law student who 'has remained simple, modest, unaffected, and unassuming.' He closed by reciting the 1995 vow he made upon SC entry without prior judicial or public office: 'I hold office by God's grace, and I pledge to serve Him and our people with fortitude, integrity, competence, and prudence. I dedicate all that I am, and all that I will ever be, to Him who is the Source of everything.' To God Be the Glory!
